microtopics.title: Ray Optics, Reflection & Refraction
entry_assumptions: **Cartesian Sign Convention Precondition**: All distances are measured from the optical pole/center. Distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive; opposite to incident light are negative. Heights upward from principal axis are positive; downward are negative.

**Paraxial Ray Approximation**: Spherical mirror formula $\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$ and lens formula $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f}$ hold strictly for rays close to and making small angles with the principal axis ($\sin\theta \approx \tan\theta \approx \theta$).
microtopics.inferential_jump: Specular reflection: incident ray, reflected ray, and surface normal lie in the same plane; angle of incidence equals angle of reflection ($\theta_i = \theta_r$).

teaching_path.action: Transverse magnification: $m = -\frac{v}{u} = \frac{h_i}{h_o}$. Real inverted images have $m < 0$; virtual erect images have $m > 0$.
Principal ray tracing algorithm: (1) Ray parallel to axis reflects through focus, (2) Ray through focus reflects parallel to axis, (3) Ray through center of curvature retraces path.
Identifying virtual objects where converging incident rays strike an optical element before meeting.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Claiming a camera cannot record an image in a plane mirror because the image is virtual.
misconceptions.repair: A virtual image acts as a real divergence source for the camera's converging lens, which projects a real image onto the camera sensor.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Believing that covering the top half of a concave mirror makes only the bottom half of the object visible.
misconceptions.repair: Every point of the object sends infinite rays to the entire mirror surface. Covering half the mirror reduces image brightness by 50% without altering the complete field of view.
